name: The Barcid Road: the Western Mediterranean, 218–201 BC

events.name: The march from New Carthage
events.summary: Hannibal crosses the Ebro, subdues the tribes to the Pyrenees and leaves Hanno to hold the new country.

events.name: The Pyrenees crossed
events.summary: The army passes the Pyrenees by the coast and buys its way through the Gauls of Ruscino.

events.name: Crossing of the Rhône
events.summary: Hanno's flanking column breaks the Volcae; Scipio lands at Massalia three days too late.

events.name: Scipio sends his army to Iberia
events.summary: Publius sends his consular army on to Iberia under Gnaeus and returns to take command in the Po valley.

events.name: Crossing of the Alps
events.summary: Fifteen days in the passes. The column descends to the Taurini with half the men it set out with, and storms their town.

events.name: Battle of Cissa
events.summary: Gnaeus Scipio destroys Hanno's army near Tarraco and takes the country north of the Ebro.

events.name: Battle of the Ticinus
events.summary: The Numidians ride round Scipio's screen; the consul is carried wounded from the field and falls back on Placentia. Clastidium's granary is betrayed to Hannibal.

events.name: Sempronius recalled from Sicily
events.summary: The invasion of Africa is abandoned; Sempronius marches the length of Italy to join his colleague.

events.name: Battle of the Trebia
events.summary: Sempronius wades the freezing river into Mago's ambush. Ten thousand legionaries cut their way out to Placentia; the Gauls of the Po rise for Carthage.

events.name: Storming of Victumulae
events.summary: The fortified market of the Insubrian plain falls to assault; Hannibal winters among his new Gallic allies.

events.name: The consuls of 217 take the field
events.summary: Rome guards both roads south: Flaminius at Arretium, Servilius at Ariminum.

events.name: Battle of Lake Trasimene
events.summary: The consular army is trapped in the morning mist between the hills and the lake; Flaminius dies with fifteen thousand men, and Maharbal destroys Servilius's cavalry.

events.name: Fabius named dictator
events.summary: Rome names a dictator. Fabius takes four legions and refuses battle.

events.name: Hannibal marches to Apulia
events.summary: Repulsed at Spoletium, Hannibal turns down the Adriatic; Fabius shadows him from the hills by Aecae.

events.name: The Falernian raid and the oxen at Callicula
events.summary: Hannibal burns the Falernian plain, slips Fabius's trap by night behind a herd of burning oxen and takes Gerunium for his winter granary.

events.name: Rome raises eight legions
events.summary: The largest army Rome has ever fielded marches into Apulia; Hannibal, his ranks filled with Gallic and Italian recruits, seizes the depot at Cannae.

events.name: Battle of Cannae
events.summary: The double envelopment. Paullus and some fifty thousand Romans fall; Varro gathers the survivors at Venusia, and the south of Italy begins to waver.

events.name: Capua goes over to Hannibal
events.summary: The second city of Italy opens its gates; Hannibal winters in Campania.

events.name: Syracuse breaks with Rome
events.summary: Hiero's heirs take Syracuse over to Carthage; Marcellus crosses to Sicily.

events.name: Fall of Syracuse
events.summary: After two years against Archimedes' engines, Marcellus storms Syracuse.

events.name: Tarentum betrayed
events.summary: Tarentine conspirators open the gates by night; the Roman garrison holds out in the citadel.

events.name: The Scipios fall in Iberia
events.summary: Divided, both Scipio brothers are destroyed on the upper Baetis; the survivors hold the Ebro line.

events.name: Hannibal marches on Rome; Capua falls
events.summary: Hannibal marches to the gates of Rome to draw off the besiegers. They do not move. Capua surrenders, and Hannibal falls back into Bruttium.

events.name: Scipio takes command in Iberia
events.summary: The son of the consul of 218 is given his father's command.

events.name: Capture of New Carthage
events.summary: Scipio wades the lagoon at ebb tide and takes the Barcid capital, its silver and its hostages in a single day.

events.name: Fabius recovers Tarentum
events.summary: The garrison that held the citadel for three years is relieved; Fabius takes the city by treachery from within.

events.name: Hasdrubal marches to Italy
events.summary: Beaten at Baecula, Hasdrubal slips north round Scipio, crosses the Alps and recruits in Gaul.

events.name: Battle of the Metaurus
events.summary: Nero's forced march joins the two consular armies; Hasdrubal dies on the Metaurus and his head is thrown into Hannibal's camp.

events.name: Battle of Ilipa
events.summary: Scipio's reversed deployment breaks Hasdrubal Gisco. Carthage loses Iberia, and Masinissa changes sides.

events.name: Scipio lands in Africa
events.summary: The Cannae legions, exiled to Sicily, sail with Scipio for Utica.

events.name: Battle of the Great Plains
events.summary: Syphax is taken; Masinissa enters Cirta as king and Scipio camps at Tunes within sight of Carthage.

events.name: Hannibal recalled from Italy
events.summary: After fifteen years in Italy Hannibal sails from Croton and lands at Hadrumetum with his veterans.

events.name: Battle of Zama
events.summary: The elephants run down Scipio's lanes, the Numidian horse return in time, and the Carthaginian army is destroyed.

events.name: Peace of 201 BC
events.summary: Carthage gives up her fleet, her elephants and Iberia, and may make no war without Rome's leave.
